title: Gila Cliff Dwellings National Monument: Secure trash and food
summary: Pack it in, pack it out! There are no trash services in or around the monument. All food & trash must be secured inside a vehicle. Ravens routinely open zipped bags & tear into trash bags left outside or in the bed of a truck.

title: Fort Bowie National Historic Site: Fort Bowie Visitor Center Bookstore is now cashless!
summary: For your convenience, we accept all major credit and debit cards, as well as mobile payment options. Electronic payment reduces transaction times, save money, and improves accountability. Thank you for your understanding and continued support!

title: Fort Bowie National Historic Site: Butterfield Trail closed to horses and pack animals.

title: Gila Cliff Dwellings National Monument: No Pets are allowed on the Cliff Dwelling Trail
summary: Pets are not allowed onto the Gila Cliff Dwelling Trail. Kennels are available at the Trailhead on a First Come First Serve basis and are available to those that are going on the Cliff Dwelling Trail not the Wilderness trails.

title: Chiricahua National Park: Vehicle Length & Trailer Restrictions
summary: No large vehicle turnaround after Faraway Ranch Parking (1 mile after entrance). Vehicles over 29 feet park at Faraway. Disconnect trailers at Faraway. Trailers with campground reservations proceed to camp. Scenic drive = 24 ft limit and no trailers.

title: Gila Cliff Dwellings National Monument: Water Availability
summary: There is NO water at the scorpion campgrounds and the trailhead for the cliff dwellings. Water is available at the Visitor Center, Woody's corral and TJ's corral.

title: Blue Creek Wilderness Study Area
summary: The Blue Creek WSA is located in the southwestern portion of New Mexico and is dominated by a volcanic fault block mountain named Black Mountain. The intermittent Blue Creek passes through the eastern part of the WSA and the narrow cliff-walled canyon is dominated by ash, cottonwood, Arizona sycamore, and willow. The uplands are dominated by desert grasses and shrubs.

title: Chiricahua National Park
summary: Explore rhyolite pinnacles and balanced rocks on foot or by car. Relax at the campground under star-filled, dark skies. See how a mountain range rising between two deserts creates a home for diverse wildlife. Imagine history here. Prehistoric peoples, Apaches, Buffalo Soldiers, Civilian Conservation Corps, ranchers, and homesteaders inhabited Chiricahua.

title: Chiricahua National Park

title: Dankworth Village
summary: Take a trip back in time and see how the Mogollon people became successful farmers in southeastern Arizona. The Paleo-Indian (Clovis culture) hunters used stone-tipped spears, and Cochise people hunted and gathered throughout the year. From Dankworth Pond State Park , the Dos Arroyos Trail leads to the Dankworth Village Trail.

title: Fort Bowie National Historic Site
summary: For nearly 25 years, Fort Bowie stood at the crossroads of the Chiricahua Apache's fight to defend their ancestral homeland and the U.S. Army's westward expansion. Today, visitors embark on a 3-mile scenic loop trail traversing the ground where this profound cultural collision forever altered the course of both American and Indigenous history.

title: Gila Cliff Dwellings National Monument
summary: For thousands of years, groups of nomads used the caves above Cliff Dweller Creek as temporary shelter. In the late 1200s, people of the agricultural Mogollon (Southern Ancestral Pueblo) culture made it a home. They built rooms, crafted pottery and raised children in the cliff dwellings for one or two generations. By approximately 1300, the Mogollon had moved on, leaving the walls behind.

title: Peloncillo Mountains Wilderness Study Area
summary: The Peloncillo Mountains WSA is in southwestern New Mexico and contiguous with the Peloncillo Wilderness in Arizona. The landform is comprised of low mountains, cliffs, and numerous canyons, with gentle hills covered in desert grasses and shrubs. Desert bighorn sheep inhabit the Peloncillo Mountains as well as Gila monsters and pincushion cacti.

title: Round Mountain Rockhound Area
summary: The Round Mountain Rockhound Area is a popular rockhounding area located near the town of Duncan in eastern Arizona. Please follow all rules and regulations when rockhounding .

title: Safford-Morenci Trail
summary: The Safford-Morenci Trail is an 18-mile historic backcountry route that offers a rugged and remote adventure through eastern Arizona. Climbing from 3,700 to 6,200 feet, the trail crosses the Gila Mountains and Turtle Mountain, showcasing desert vistas and riparian corridors. title: San Simon Valley
summary: Approximately 500,000 acres of public land in the San Simon Valley provide a variety of recreational opportunities. The Hot Well Dunes Recreation Area is located in the heart of the San Simon Valley. This Special Recreation Management Area provides unique opportunities for off-highway vehicle riding and hot-water soaking. Wildlife species in the area include quail, dove, deer, and javelina.

title: Willcox Playa National Natural Landmark
